_notes.matching: priority and exclusion terms are substring-matched after accent folding and lowercasing (hunter.text_key), so an accented duplicate of an existing term is a no-op and a short term can match inside an unrelated word.
_notes.exclusion_terms_are_hard_rejects: hunter.is_meaningful() returns False whenever evaluate() produced any exclusion, so every entry in exclusion_terms is a hard reject and its weight only shapes the displayed fit score. Only unambiguous, property-level disqualifiers belong here. Ambiguous prose is left to the evidence-backed structured fields: large_development, units, expenses_ars, needs_major_renovation, high_traffic, security_concern.
_notes.priority_a_search_slots: hunter.research_plan() puts only the FIRST SEVEN priority_a_terms into the generated Priority A query, so entries 1-7 are ordered for search value and the later entries are spelling variants and landmarks kept for matching only.
_notes.priority_terms_are_the_discovery_gate: fetch_ml.relevant() drops any swept record that matches no priority term, so a missing area name silently discards listings rather than merely downgrading them.
_notes.price_bands: ideal_price_usd and strong_price_usd are documentation; the 300k and 350k band edges are hardcoded in hunter.evaluate(). Keep them in sync by hand.
_notes.peso_thresholds_drift: expenses_review_ars and expenses_reject_ars are nominal pesos, so Argentine inflation erodes them into hard rejects of ordinary listings. Re-check both against observed expensas in current Beccar and San Isidro listings before trusting them; they were not re-verified in this pass.
